minutes.headline: Planning Board nearly finished the stormwater bylaw update, aiming for fall Town Meeting; LID bylaw deferred.
minutes.summary: The remote Planning Board meeting centered on the Chapter 204 stormwater bylaw update, with a debate over whether to set stricter, "future-proofed" design numbers or follow federal and state requirements so it passes Town Meeting. The board agreed to add language that the building inspector not issue a permit without confirming whether a stormwater permit is needed. It also approved two sets of minutes by roll call, heard committee reports, and discussed workshop scheduling. A resident complaint about a permitted project was raised for a future agenda.

budget_items.what_was_said: Documents to authorize the study are with the town manager for signature, and money has been authorized. The Donahue Institute lead expects completion by year end.
A member worried that weak bylaw standards could cost taxpayers more later to fix problems.
The committee must develop a cost estimate for town offices, school and community uses, complicated by the unclear Boys and Girls Club space needs and the traffic study.

decisions.decision: Add Westminster-style language to the stormwater bylaw that the building inspector will not issue a building permit without confirming whether a stormwater permit is required, placed in the enforcement section.
Board expects to wrap up the stormwater bylaw in the next two meetings for the early-September warrant; LID bylaw will not go to fall Town Meeting.
Director to draw up a 2021 meeting calendar with the first meeting of odd months as workshops; Sept 14 to be the first workshop.
Next meeting Aug 24 will take up the scenic road and common driveway applications together.
A resident complaint about a permitted stormwater/site plan project will be put on a future agenda, with a broader review of permit conditions and communication among departments.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board worked through the Chapter 204 stormwater bylaw update and expects to finish it in two meetings for the early-September warrant.
The proposed low-impact development (LID) bylaw will not go to the fall Town Meeting.
The board agreed to add language that the building inspector will not issue a building permit without confirming whether a stormwater permit is required.
A resident complaint about a permitted project will go on a future agenda, with a wider review of permit conditions and communication among departments.
The board set Aug 24 to take up the scenic road and common driveway applications together, and Sept 14 as its first workshop.

why_it_matters: The stormwater bylaw sets the rules for how new building handles runoff, and a weaker standard could shift repair costs to taxpayers later, a concern raised in the discussion.
Residents will likely be asked to vote on the bylaw at the fall Town Meeting, while the LID bylaw is pushed to a later round.
watch_next: Aug 24 Planning Board meeting: scenic road and common driveway applications, plus further stormwater bylaw edits.
Sept 14 workshop, and the fall Town Meeting warrant, where the stormwater bylaw is expected.
